_comment: The gates `pnpm verify` runs, in order, as DATA rather than as one shell
string joined by `&&`.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `package.json` used to hold the whole chain:
pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint:rust && pnpm test && ... && cargo test --workspace --locked
That string is a correct chain and a useless report. `&&` short-circuits, so
on a machine without cargo on PATH the run dies inside gate 2 and prints one
ELIFECYCLE line; gates 3 through 10 never execute and nothing anywhere says
so. `src/platform/verify-covers-ci.test.ts` was green the whole time,
because it asked whether the gate's TEXT appeared in that string — a
question the string answers yes to whether or not the process ever ran.
Structured data lets the runner report a per-gate verdict, and lets the
superset guard assert over fields instead of regexing a shell line.
FIELDS
id       stable name; what the report and the tests refer to.
command  the literal command line. Repo text, never caller input; the
runner passes it to a shell because `pnpm` is a shim on Windows.
cwd      relative to the repository root.
needs    external tools that must resolve before the run starts. The
runner PREFLIGHTS these so a missing toolchain is reported as a
missing toolchain, not as gate 2 failing for reasons unknown.
tail     true for the gates whose execution is proved afterwards by
`scripts/check-rust-tail.mjs` rather than by their exit code.
tailProbe is not a gate. It is the check the runner performs AFTER the
gate marked `tail`, with a `--since` sentinel taken when the run started,
to establish that the Rust tail physically executed rather than merely
reporting a status. It is declared here rather than hardcoded in the runner
so that `verify-covers-ci.test.ts` can see it: CI runs the same script as a
step of its own, and a CI step no local command reaches is the defect that
file exists to prevent.
READERS: `scripts/verify.mjs` executes this list;
`src/platform/verify-covers-ci.test.ts` asserts it covers every gate in
`.github/workflows/`; `src/platform/verify-runner.test.ts` drives the runner
with a synthetic copy of this shape.
